correctness.rationale: Private-leaf domination and independence force every independent dominating set to be a transversal of every root–leaf pair. The resulting exactly-twice-covered index supports imply precisely four partition classes. A bipartite perfect matching in the two-by-two coalition-partner graph forces two complementary independent dominating sets, hence bipartiteness of the base. Conversely a bipartition permits four classes. Counting unordered complementary colorings and nonempty bipartitions, then subtracting only those partitions with both cross matchings as valid coalitions, gives the coefficient. Exhaustive adjacency-level independent enumeration of all partitions for 82 base graphs checks every cardinality, including nonbipartite and disconnected cases, but is not an unbounded proof.

originality.rationale: The 2023 foundational arXiv paper defines independent coalition partitions and poses the existence question; Proposition 4.8 already gives a general bipartite necessity for four-class partitions without isolates or full vertices, and that particular implication is excluded from the novelty claim. The 2026 counting preprint covers a special connected tree family and its implications are likewise credited. Neither inspected complete text states the arbitrary-base corona iff criterion, enforced four classes, or exact disconnected correction. Seven actual semantic database queries returned related different domination/general-position results, not a covering ICP corona theorem. The plausible 2025 journal work was not accessible in full and remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: An exact graph-family classification for when independent-coalition partitions exist, complete rigidity of class number and nontrivial component-corrected enumeration, extending across all connected cyclic bipartite bases and all disconnected or nonbipartite bases. This directly addresses the cited existence question and identifies a subtle two-presentation counting obstruction absent from naive 2-coloring enumeration; it is not just re-labeling a familiar tree count.
